state:
Goal `core-process-and-4-more`. `Core\Process` is green. `Core\Process\Handle` has its class card, and `kill` and `readStdout` have all their feature proofs. `readStderr`, `writeStdin` and `wait` still owe everything but their cards, and those cards are still in the old voice. `Core\Process\Result`, `Core\Program` and `Core\Queue` are untouched and still in `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`.

The `readStdout` attack found a memory-limit bypass, fixed in the same slice. A `nvs_host::blocking::run` or `pin` answer was allocated on a pool thread and freed on the core, so the request's balance went negative and a program keeping every answer ran past `[limits] memory`. `nvs_runtime::budget::carry` now moves the charge across (the `budget` module doc's *Per thread* section and `run`'s doc own it). The `bg.test.ts` floor check was flaky under load, not broken. Its listing test now waits for a release file, and `job.json`'s second write is atomic.

A Unix-only example is run by hand under WSL. Put the commands in a script under `.agent-tmp/` and start it with `wsl.exe -- bash -lc "bash <script>"`: a plain `bash <script>` has no `cargo` on its PATH, and `bash -lc` with the commands inline mangles nested quotes. In the script, build with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl cargo build` from `/mnt/d/mwl`, run `/var/tmp/nvs-target-wsl/debug/nvs run --config <dir>/nvs.toml <file>`, write the `.out` from that run and `cmp` it. The attacks and benches run on both platforms: they pick `/bin/echo` / `/usr/bin/yes` or `cmd.exe` by `Core\Path::SEPARATOR`. `benches/members/core/Process-Handle/nvs.toml` is shared by every bench in its class. `?bytes` narrows through `!= null` in a `while` or `if` head, not through `&&`.

Rewrite `READ_STDERR_DOC` in the plain voice, the way `READ_STDOUT_DOC` now reads. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/process.rs:392`

backlog: `Core\Program` and `Core\Queue`: class cards and every member's proofs — `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/program.rs`, `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/queue.rs`.

A child blocked on a full standard-error pipe while the program waits in `readStdout` never returns. PHP's `proc_open` behaves the same; not checked whether a request's time limit ends that wait — `rule:core-classes/process-spawn`.
